Conventional quantum notion: Linear combination of amplitudes, with normalization and rays
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Nonzero vector addition. F2 already suffices; a state added to itself gives zero, which is not a state
Important missing feature: No continuous amplitudes, norm, or constructive intensity

Conventional quantum notion: Scalar unit-modulus factors; relative phases become observable after mixing
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: F2 scalar phase is trivial. A has units, including R of order four; relative diagonal units plus a shear change support
Important missing feature: R is unipotent, not a diagonalizable complex quarter turn; phase depends on coarse readout

Conventional quantum notion: A target eigenvalue becomes a control-dependent phase
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: In shared A-coefficient theory, Boolean XOR kicks back z=R^2 using (1,z); R uses a four-level cyclic target and a separately declared oracle
Important missing feature: Eigenvectors do not form a Fourier basis; standard bit flip cannot have a primitive R-eigenvector

Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: W^2=I and W diag(I,R^k) W(v,0)=(v,v+R^k v). Destructive cancellation is exactly XOR cancellation
Important missing feature: No amplitude magnitude, fringes with intensities, or Born statistics

Conventional quantum notion: Incompatible observables and incompatible outcome statistics
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Distinct complete dual bases Z, X, Y of F2^2 already give deterministic versus ambiguous outcomes
Important missing feature: These are not Hilbert mutually unbiased bases; they can share effect rays

Conventional quantum notion: A pure state is not a product across a specified partition
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Over a field, coefficient rank >=2. Over the chain ring, at least two nonzero Smith factors
Important missing feature: S and L have different products and different separability tests

Conventional quantum notion: No local model reproduces the pattern of possible events
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: A finite support model is nonlocal iff some possible event fails to extend to a global assignment
Important missing feature: No Bell expectation value, violation magnitude, or experimental probability

Conventional quantum notion: A possible event and several zero probabilities contradict local predetermined outcomes
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Uniform two-setting Hardy witnesses exist for two nonzero Smith factors; unequal valuations yield logical but not strong contextuality with all A-bases
Important missing feature: This exact pure-state intermediate stratum depends on ring valuation and measurement contract

Conventional quantum notion: No global assignment is compatible with the support
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Already present in F2 Bell states with Z, X, Y; over complete chain-ring bases it is determined by lowest-valuation multiplicity >=2
Important missing feature: Not a generic consequence of a four-cycle phase group

Conventional quantum notion: All-or-nothing multipartite constraints, conventionally a four-context parity argument
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: The state 000+111 has a no-global-assignment support table for three local F2 bases; phase-expanded literal GHZ has the corresponding coarse table
Important missing feature: For every state in the binary contracts studied here, at most two settings per site always admit a global assignment (R1b); the conventional two-setting GHZ pattern is unavailable

Conventional quantum notion: No physical map copies an arbitrary unknown pure state
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Linearity and tensor composition forbid v -> v tensor v on all nonzero F2 vectors when d>=2
Important missing feature: Classical descriptions and basis labels remain copyable

Conventional quantum notion: Reversible dynamics cannot erase one unknown copy without moving the information elsewhere
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Reversible deletion with a fixed blank and no information-bearing environment is impossible
Important missing feature: A noninvertible diagonal contraction deletes duplicated F2 vectors algebraically, but is not automatically a complete deterministic operation

Conventional quantum notion: Entanglement plus classical feed-forward transfers an unknown state
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Complete invertible-matrix effect bases and inverse branch corrections give exact protocols; universal resource must be invertible
Important missing feature: No probabilities or fidelity. Literal 8-dimensional teleportation needs 64 outcomes and unrestricted phase operations beyond the native A-linear analyzer

Conventional quantum notion: Entanglement increases distinguishable messages for a transmitted carrier
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Field resource of rank r: d*r invertible-orbit codewords. Shared chain ring: d*h block messages
Important missing feature: Exact distinguishability is not Shannon capacity. Nilpotent dense coding need not imply universal teleportation

Conventional quantum notion: A joint measurement connects two remote entangled resources
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Coefficient contraction M E N; invertible resources and invertible reshaped effects preserve full rank, with local correction
Important missing feature: No heralding probability; the allowed analyzer must be specified

Conventional quantum notion: A known target state is prepared remotely using shared correlations
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Over a field, a heralded branch prepares phi iff phi is in im(M^T); over A the allowed projective effect must have a primitive preimage
Important missing feature: Possibility is not guaranteed occurrence; no optimal communication advantage is established

Conventional quantum notion: A code reverses a declared error channel on an unknown state
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: An exact distinguishable-syndrome construction exists when error images are injective and form a direct sum; a 3-mobit repetition example works coherently
Important missing feature: No noise probabilities, thresholds, CPTP channels, or general Knill-Laflamme replacement

Conventional quantum notion: Pauli normalizers admit efficient state/effect tableaus
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: A is a principled equivariant linear algebra, and a genuine Pauli-like finite group exists; its actual normalizer is much smaller than the native gate set
Important missing feature: Finiteness or matrix linearity does not imply simulation polynomial in the number of carriers

Conventional quantum notion: Coherent queries, phase processing and readout yield task-dependent query bounds
Exact Boolean/modal analogue and result: Reversible Boolean oracles exist. Deutsch/DJ one-query forms fail; BV needs n queries; known modal UNIQUE-SAT succeeds in one query
Important missing feature: A CM implementation on a classical machine is not thereby a faster physical oracle
